referenceFunction.generalComment: The module roughly describes the net electricity production of an average 20 MW plant for self-generation in major coal mines in the country. For the main characteristics (LHV, sulphur and ash content of coal, efficiency of the plant) and key criteria emissions (SOx and particles), direct information from individual Shandong and Shanxi major coal mines around 2000 from the CETP project (Dones, Zhou and Tian 2003) has been used. These base data have been integrated for other species as well as trace elements and radionuclides using maximum data from European plants (see corresponding meta-information). The waste heat releases to air and water have been allocated on the basis of the assumed share of water cooled power plants and assumptions on the direct losses to air as for major European plants (no data available specific to China). The ash (assumed 50% of input coal) is assumed to be all disposed using the corresponding dataset for Poland (lack of information specific to characteristics of ash disposal within Chinese mines).; UUID: d838d412-0c1f-371b-bb52-daf1cedea15b
referenceFunction.includedProcesses: Energy conversion for electricity production. Use of fuel oil for startup is accounted for. Particle removal is included in this module. DeSOx and DeNOx are not explicitly included (some of these units use Fluidized Bed Combustion technology, but data on SO2 emissions emissions comes from major coal mines in Shandong and Shanxi, which cover this case as well). Along with major units, it is assumed that 25 % of the plants are river cooled, 75 % use cooling tower (average UCTE; average specific conditions in Chinese coal mines are not known). The water treatment is described in separate modules. The disposal of ashes, entirely assumed non-recycled, is modelled separately.
